gaps.sentence: 'Well done, you've passed!' the examiner said. The examiner ___ me on passing.
'I have to catch the last train,' she said. She said she ___ catch the last train.
gaps.explanation: Have to (obligation) backshifts to had to after a past reporting verb.

gaps.sentence: They ___ breaking the window, but nobody believed them.
gaps.explanation: Deny + -ing reports a rejection of the accusation; 'but nobody believed them' confirms the meaning.

gaps.sentence: 'You can rely on me,' she assured me. She assured me that I ___ rely on her.
gaps.explanation: Can backshifts to could after the past reporting verb 'assured'.

gaps.sentence: 'You really ought to try the tasting menu,' the waiter said. The waiter ___ trying the tasting menu.
gaps.explanation: Recommend takes a gerund (recommend doing) when there is no object.

gaps.sentence: He ___ me his car for the weekend.
gaps.explanation: Offer takes the double-object pattern (offer somebody something); the others do not.

gaps.sentence: 'We won't stay long,' they said. They said they ___ stay long.
gaps.explanation: will not → would not (wouldn't) after a past reporting verb.

gaps.sentence: 'Why did you cancel the order?' he asked. He asked why I ___ the order.
gaps.explanation: Wh-questions keep the wh-word but drop do-support and backshift: did you cancel → I had cancelled.
